claims.title: Pearling and fishing villages on the Gulf coast
claims.summary: The peninsula's people lived from pearl diving, fishing and seasonal Bedouin herding, with pearls the great export carried across the Indian Ocean and Arabia from the early Islamic period and earlier.

sources.label: Persian Gulf States: Country Studies (Qatar)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Founding of Al Zubarah
claims.summary: Families migrating from Kuwait, including the Al Khalifa, settled the northwest coast and built Al Zubarah, which grew into a flourishing walled pearling and trading town.

sources.label: Al Zubarah: Qatar's Largest Heritage Site
Persian Gulf States: Country Studies (Qatar)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Destruction of Al Zubarah
claims.summary: After attacks by rival Gulf powers, the thriving town of Al Zubarah was burned to the ground; it fell into decline and was abandoned by the early 20th century.

sources.label: Al Zubarah: Qatar's Largest Heritage Site

claims.title: Bahraini attack and the Qatari-Bahraini conflict
claims.summary: Forces from Bahrain and its allies attacked Al Wakrah and Al Bidda, an assault the British viewed as a breach of Gulf agreements and that sharpened Qatar's sense of separate identity.

sources.label: Sheikh Mohammed bin Thani — Qatar's Rulers
sources.publisher: The Amiri Diwan, State of Qatar

claims.title: British agreement with Sheikh Mohammed bin Thani
claims.summary: Colonel Lewis Pelly concluded a separate agreement with Mohammed bin Thani, widely taken to mark Qatar's emergence as a distinct entity and the rise of Al Thani rule.

sources.label: Sheikh Mohammed bin Thani — Qatar's Rulers
sources.publisher: The Amiri Diwan, State of Qatar

claims.title: Ottoman garrison established
claims.summary: The Ottoman Empire extended its presence into eastern Arabia and placed a garrison on the Qatari peninsula, beginning several decades of nominal Ottoman authority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Qatar: From pearling shores and Bedouin tribes to a gas-rich peninsula state and global stage.", terralore.co/country/QAT/chronicle#ev-1871-ottoman-garrison-established, claim TL:QAT:event:1871:ottoman-garrison-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sheikh Jassim succeeds as ruler
claims.summary: Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani formally succeeded his father, an event commemorated as Qatar's National Day and marking the consolidation of the tribes under Al Thani leadership.

sources.label: Sheikh Mohammed bin Thani — Qatar's Rulers
sources.publisher: The Amiri Diwan, State of Qatar

claims.title: Battle of Al Wajba
claims.summary: Sheikh Jassim's tribal forces defeated an Ottoman expedition at Al Wajba, forcing the release of Qatari captives in a victory remembered as a key assertion of Qatari autonomy.

claims.title: Anglo-Qatari Treaty: British protectorate
claims.summary: Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim signed a treaty (ratified 1918) placing Qatar under British protection in exchange for foregoing relations and concessions with other powers without British consent.

sources.label: Text of the Treaty of 3 November 1916 between His Majesty's Government and Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim of al-Katar
sources.publisher: Qatar Digital Library / British Library India Office Records

claims.title: First oil concession signed
claims.summary: Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim granted an oil concession, opening Qatar to the exploration that would lead to the discovery of oil within a few years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Qatar: From pearling shores and Bedouin tribes to a gas-rich peninsula state and global stage.", terralore.co/country/QAT/chronicle#ev-1935-first-oil-concession-signed, claim TL:QAT:event:1935:first-oil-concession-signed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oil discovered at Dukhan
claims.summary: Following the 1935 concession, oil was discovered at the Dukhan field, though development stalled during the Second World War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Qatar: From pearling shores and Bedouin tribes to a gas-rich peninsula state and global stage.", terralore.co/country/QAT/chronicle#ev-1939-oil-discovered-at-dukhan, claim TL:QAT:event:1939:oil-discovered-at-dukhan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First oil exports begin
claims.summary: Commercial export of Dukhan crude began in 1949, starting the transformation of an economy battered by the collapse of the pearl trade in the 1930s.

sources.label: Persian Gulf States: Country Studies (Qatar)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Independence from Britain
claims.summary: Qatar declared independence from Great Britain, ending the protectorate established in 1916; the United States recognised the new State of Qatar on 5 September 1971.

sources.label: A Guide to U.S. Recognition and Diplomatic Relations: Qatar
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa takes power
claims.summary: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani became emir in 1995, launching reforms and the development of Qatar's natural gas wealth that would make it one of the richest states in the world.

claims.title: Al Jazeera launched
claims.summary: Qatar founded Al Jazeera, the first independent Arabic-language satellite news channel, broadcasting from Doha and giving the small state global reach and influence.

sources.label: Sheikh Hamad ibn Khalifa Al Thani

claims.title: North Field LNG development
claims.summary: Qatar invested heavily in liquefied natural gas from its offshore North Field, becoming the world's leading LNG exporter and reaching among the highest per-capita incomes globally.

claims.title: Hamad abdicates in favour of Tamim
claims.summary: In a transfer of power unusual for the Gulf, Sheikh Hamad abdicated in favour of his son Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, then 33, to make way for a new generation.

sources.label: Sheikh Hamad ibn Khalifa Al Thani
Sheikh Tamim ibn Hamad Al Thani

claims.title: Sheikh Tamim becomes emir
claims.summary: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani succeeded his father as emir of Qatar, having earlier overseen the country's successful bid to host the 2022 World Cup.

claims.title: Blockade by neighbouring states
claims.summary: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt cut ties and imposed a land, sea and air blockade, accusing Qatar of supporting terrorism; Qatar rejected their thirteen demands as a breach of its sovereignty.

claims.summary: At the GCC summit in Al Ula, the parties signed a solidarity and stability agreement restoring relations and reopening routes, ending the nearly four-year dispute.

claims.summary: Qatar staged the FIFA World Cup, the first in an Arab and Muslim country, after a decade of major infrastructure investment, drawing both global celebration and scrutiny.
